verdict: STOP — the pre-registered kill criterion fired. `jac` does not beat `shuffled` on either held-out sequence, and is the worst of three arms on near-rim on both.

arms.shuffled: same values, fixed permutation of token positions
arms.theta: theta only, zero-padded to equal width

design.held_fixed: architecture, parameter count (LoRA 122.9k + FiLM 25.5k), data, seed, optimiser, loss
design.loss: PLAIN depth loss (alpha=0) — rim weighting is what lost to its control in H5

the_one_thing_that_is_not_nothing: on decoration_seq132 the arms differ far more in the CENTRE than at the rim, and there jac is much the best (centre +0.31% vs shuffled +16.73%; near-centre +29.97% vs +57.49%). The conditioning is not inert — it protects the centre rather than helping the rim. Reported because it is real, not as a salvaged result; it was not pre-registered and it does not rescue the hypothesis.
not_claimed: One seed, one run per arm; margins are small (5% relative on seq136) and no error bars were computed. The stop rests on the DIRECTION plus pre-registration, not on the size of the gap.
Not that conditioning cannot work — only that FiLM on the last ViT block, at this capacity, on this data, does not.
Nothing about cross-lens transfer: that was the reason for the design and was never reached.
